what: Credo Technology makes high-speed connectivity products for data centres: active electrical cables, retimers and chiplets that move data between AI accelerators and switches at very high speed with low power use.
customers: Hyperscale cloud operators, AI infrastructure builders and networking equipment makers.
money: active electrical cables, retimers, optical digital signal processors and chiplets
moat: Active electrical cables that deliver optical-like performance at copper cost and power, designed into AI rack architectures where power per bit is the binding constraint.
risks: A handful of hyperscale customers account for most of its revenue
A slowdown in AI data centre building would hit it immediately
Larger competitors can bundle connectivity with their main chip sales
The shares trade at a very high multiple of revenue
opportunities: Revenue grew about 206% last year and about 94% a year over three years
Operating margin of 33% with return on invested capital of 21%
Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
watch: Quarterly revenue guidance and the degree of customer concentration.
